title: How To Fail At Almost Everything And Still Win Big

questions.q: Why does Adams prefer systems to goals?
a: Systems make today count and leave room to adjust
Systems guarantee that you will get rich
Systems remove the need for any planning
Systems are easier to explain to other people
questions.why: Lesson one says goals are distant and rigid, while systems let each day feel like a win and timing stop mattering.

questions.q: What two flaws does Adams see in goals?
a: They sit in the future and demand a specific outcome
They require too much money and free time
They are too easy and rarely motivating
They depend on luck and other people
questions.why: Lesson one says a goal's distant deadline is depressing and its specificity breeds disappointment even with near misses.

questions.q: How does Adams suggest finding skills you might have overlooked?
a: Notice where you are comfortable taking risks
Ask friends to list your weaknesses
Take a personality test online
Follow the career with the highest salary
questions.why: Lesson two says comfort with risk, such as enjoying public speaking, points to areas worth developing.

Working several part-time jobs at once
Shadowing a manager for a week
Taking a test to match your skills
questions.why: Lesson two describes it as experimenting with different kinds of work until something sticks.

questions.q: What three angles does Adams use to manage energy?
a: Activities, space and time
Sleep, diet and exercise
Goals, systems and habits
Money, status and freedom
questions.why: Lesson three looks at what excites or drains you, where you work best, and when your internal clock peaks.
